# Tidyup 12: Extended metadata for R package repositories

**Champion**: Gábor Csárdi<br>
**Co-champion**: TBD<br>
**Status**: Draft

## Abstract

This tidyup specifies a set of files that an R package repository can
serve, in addition to the usual `PACKAGES` files, to describe its full
history: every source package version it ever published, the packages
it removed, and every binary build of every package version. Tools that
lock or reproduce R projects need this information, and today they can
only get it by scraping several services. The format is plain DCF and
TSV, compressed with zstd, so it is easy to produce and easy to read.

Posit Package Manager (P3M) data for CRAN and Bioconductor is
published in this format at `https://ppm.r-pkg.org` and
`https://ppm-bioc.r-pkg.org`. `rig` is the reference client, and uses
these files to solve and lock `rproj.toml` projects, see
[Tidyup 9](009-rproj-toml.md) and [Tidyup 11](011-rproj-lock.md).

## Motivation

- **`PACKAGES` only describes the present.**

  A CRAN-like repository's `PACKAGES` file lists the current version of
  each package. Older versions live in `src/contrib/Archive/`, which
  has no index of its own, so a resolver cannot see their
  dependencies without downloading and unpacking every tarball. A
  dependency solver that may need to go back to an older version, for
  example to satisfy an upper bound, or to reproduce a project as it
  was on a given day, needs all of them.

- **No record of when a version was published.**

  Reproducing a project "as of" a date needs the date each version
  first appeared. `PACKAGES` does not have it. Snapshot repositories
  have it implicitly, one full `PACKAGES` file per day, but finding the
  first snapshot of a version means searching through them.

- **No record of removed packages.**

  CRAN archives packages regularly. A tool cannot tell an archived
  package from a typo, or tell the user when and why it disappeared,
  without the archive date.

- **Binaries are scattered across many `PACKAGES` files.**

  P3M serves binaries for many Linux distributions, macOS and Windows,
  for many R versions, from daily snapshots. Finding out which builds
  exist for a package means asking one `PACKAGES` file per platform, R
  version and date. A lock file that covers several platforms and R
  versions needs all of those answers at once.

- **Binaries depend on the versions they were built against.**

  A binary of a package with `LinkingTo` dependencies includes code
  from the headers of those dependencies. If the installed version of a
  `LinkingTo` dependency differs, the binary may not work. `PACKAGES`
  does not record which versions a binary was built against.

## Solution

A repository with extended metadata has a base URL, and serves these
files under it:

```
<base>/ALLPACKAGES.zst
<base>/ALLPACKAGES
<base>/ARCHIVEDPACKAGES.zst
<base>/ARCHIVEDPACKAGES
<base>/binaries/<package>.tsv.zst
```

The plain text files have the same content as their `.zst` counterparts.
The extended metadata does not replace the repository: package files
are still downloaded from the URLs listed in the metadata, and the
repository may still serve regular `PACKAGES` files for tools that do
not know about this format.

This format is for repositories that keep old package versions and
old binary builds available after they publish new ones. Download
URLs should be stable: the URL of a file should not change, and it
should keep working for as long as the repository serves the file.
This is not required, but it is strongly suggested, because lock
files record these URLs.

The current instances are:

| Repository | Base URL |
|---|---|
| CRAN | `https://ppm.r-pkg.org` |
| Bioconductor release `<v>` | `https://ppm-bioc.r-pkg.org/<v>`, e.g. `https://ppm-bioc.r-pkg.org/3.22` |

### `ALLPACKAGES`

`ALLPACKAGES` is a DCF file, in the same format as `PACKAGES`, with one
record for every source package version the repository ever published,
archived or not. For CRAN this is around 200,000 records.

```
Package: cli
Version: 3.6.6
Depends: R (>= 3.4)
Imports: utils
Suggests: callr, covr, crayon, digest, glue (>= 1.6.0), grDevices, htmltools, htmlwidgets, knitr, methods, processx, ps (>= 1.3.4.9000), rlang (>= 1.0.2.9003), rmarkdown, rprojroot, rstudioapi, testthat (>= 3.2.0), tibble, whoami, withr
License: MIT + file LICENSE
NeedsCompilation: yes
SHA256: 27b5e74a6b2a8264457ce8412ded40aa7b660e01894bea4bfde956bbc4b5b294
Id: b2b58d6dd82f5798b335e39c00591686a01fd3e94399ef898e146173e36f18f9
Snapshot: 2026-04-10
DownloadURL: https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-04-10/src/contrib/cli_3.6.6.tar.gz
```

Fields copied from the package's `DESCRIPTION` file, if present:

- `Package`, `Version` (always present).
- `Depends`, `Imports`, `LinkingTo`, `Suggests`, `Enhances`.
- `License`, `License_is_FOSS`, `License_restricts_use`.
- `NeedsCompilation`, `Priority`, `OS_type`, `Archs`,
  `SystemRequirements`.

Fields added by the repository, always present:

- `SHA256`: the SHA-256 hash of the file at `DownloadURL`.
- `Id`: an identifier of the source tarball, in the same format as a
  SHA-256 hash: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Different
  tarballs must have different ids, and the id of a tarball must not
  change over time. The binary indices use this id as well.

  A repository can use its `SHA256` field as the id. P3M uses the
  SHA-256 hash of the original source tarball, as published by the
  upstream repository (CRAN or Bioconductor).
- `Snapshot`: the date the version first appeared in the repository,
  as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `DownloadURL`: the download URL of the source tarball. It should
  be a stable URL, see above.

Rules for readers:

- Records are in no particular order.

- The same `(Package, Version)` pair may appear more than once. This
  happens when the upstream repository replaced a tarball without
  changing its version number. The records differ in `SHA256`,
  `Id`, `Snapshot` and `DownloadURL`, and possibly in the
  other fields. There are about 350 such pairs for CRAN. Each of these
  records is valid, and readers may use any of them.

- The file may have comment lines, starting with `#`. Readers must
  skip them.

- Some records may have dependency fields that do not parse, e.g.
  `Depends: tcltk (butonlyfortheGUI), allotherfunctionsarestandalone)`.
  Readers should skip these records, not the whole file.

### `ARCHIVEDPACKAGES`

`ARCHIVEDPACKAGES` lists the packages that the upstream repository
removed. It has the same format and the same fields as `ALLPACKAGES`,
plus one more field:

- `Archived`: the date the package was archived, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

There is one record per archived package, describing the last version
published before it was archived.

```
Package: gpclib
Version: 1.5-6
Depends: R (>= 3.0.0), methods
Imports: graphics
License: file LICENSE
License_restricts_use: yes
NeedsCompilation: yes
SHA256: 5ef1de6f69ca88b8d9960b3c637d566b59d7401aa4ec1d3dc30bb248e9126c00
Id: fa4e3e1f74e327b185e873052f826312ed6f71cc907a49be4c1e224ace7b5286
Snapshot: 2020-03-02
DownloadURL: https://p3m.dev/cran/2020-03-02/src/contrib/gpclib_1.5-6.tar.gz
Archived: 2023-04-06
```

A package is "current" if it has a record in `ALLPACKAGES` and does
not have one in `ARCHIVEDPACKAGES`. If an archived package comes back
to the upstream repository, the repository removes its record from
`ARCHIVEDPACKAGES`.

### `binaries/<package>.tsv.zst`

There is one binary index per package, a zstd-compressed,
tab-separated file. The first line is a header with the column names,
and each other line is one downloadable file: the source tarball or a
binary build.

```
package version platform       arch   r_version source-id url                                                                                     linkingto
cli     3.6.6   source         *      *         b2b58d…   https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-04-10/src/contrib/cli_3.6.6.tar.gz
cli     3.6.6   macos          arm64  4.6       b2b58d…   https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-04-10/bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.6/cli_3.6.6.tgz
cli     3.6.6   windows        x86_64 4.6       b2b58d…   https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-04-10/bin/windows/contrib/4.6/cli_3.6.6.zip
cli     3.6.6   noble          x86_64 4.6       b2b58d…   https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-04-10/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/4.6/src/contrib/cli_3.6.6.tar.gz
cli     3.6.6   manylinux_2_28 arm64  4.6       b2b58d…   https://p3m.dev/cran/2026-04-10/bin/linux/manylinux_2_28-arm64/4.6/src/contrib/cli_3.6.6.tar.gz
```

Columns:

- `package`: the package name.
- `version`: the package version, exactly as in `ALLPACKAGES`.
- `platform`: `source` for the source tarball. Otherwise `macos`,
  `windows`, a Linux distribution name, e.g. `jammy`, `noble`,
  `bookworm`, `rhel9`, `opensuse156`, or `manylinux_2_28` for a
  generic build that works on any Linux distribution with glibc 2.28
  or later.
- `arch`: `*` for source tarballs, otherwise `x86_64` or `arm64`
  (not `aarch64`).
- `r_version`: `*` for source tarballs, otherwise the minor R version
  the binary was built for, e.g. `4.5`.
- `source-id`: the `Id` of the source tarball of the
  version, from `ALLPACKAGES`. It is the same on every row of a
  version. It is *not* the hash of the file at `url`, so it cannot be
  used to check a download, use `sha256` or `md5` for that. It
  identifies the source tarball the binary was built from.
- `url`: the download URL of the file. It should be a stable URL,
  see above.
- `sha256`: the SHA-256 hash of the file at `url`.
- `md5`: the MD5 hash of the file at `url`.
- `linkingto`: empty for source tarballs and for packages without
  `LinkingTo` dependencies. Otherwise the source versions of the
  `LinkingTo` dependencies the binary was built against, as a
  comma-separated list of `<package>@<version>=<id>` entries,
  where `<id>` is the `Id` of that dependency
  version:

  ```
  cpp11@0.5.4=6e0053ce…,systemfonts@1.3.2=828a1780…,textshaping@1.0.5=12209d55…
  ```

  This list is the transitive closure of `LinkingTo` dependencies, not
  a copy of the package's `LinkingTo` field. E.g. ragg has
  `LinkingTo: systemfonts, textshaping`, and its list also includes
  cpp11, because systemfonts and textshaping link to it.

Rules for readers:

- Find columns by their name in the header, not by their position.
  New columns may be added later. The `linkingto`, `sha256` and `md5`
  columns are optional. An index may have `sha256`, `md5`, both, or
  neither.

- In the `sha256` and `md5` columns a missing value is the string
  `NA`. Clients cannot check the download of a file if both `sha256` and
  `md5` are missing.

- Several rows may have the same `version`, `platform`, `arch` and
  `r_version`. This happens when a package was rebuilt because a
  `LinkingTo` dependency changed, and the `linkingto` column is what
  tells them apart. A client that picks a binary for a lock file needs
  to pick the row whose `linkingto` versions match the versions it
  resolved, or fall back to the source tarball.

- A package without an index, e.g. a Bioconductor package in the CRAN
  repository, has no file, so an HTTP(S) server returns 404.

There is no index of all binaries, and no listing of the `binaries/`
directory. Clients download the indices of the packages they need, one
request per package.

## Implementations

### Server

The CRAN and Bioconductor instances are generated from P3M data and
updated daily. They use slightly different `ALLPACKAGES` keys and
different column names in the binary tables currently, this will be
standardized as the this specification matures.

### `rig`

`rig` uses the extended metadata for:

- solving dependencies, using all versions in `ALLPACKAGES`, not just
  the current ones;
- `--exclude-newer <date>`: hiding the versions with a `Snapshot`
  date after `<date>`;
- listing available packages, hiding archived packages, and telling the
  user when a package was archived;
- picking binaries for each target of a lock file, matching `platform`,
  `arch`, `r_version` and `linkingto`;
- recording `Id` in the lock file and in installed
  packages, to tell whether an installed package is the same as the
  locked one.

## Backwards compatibility

The extended metadata is served in addition to the regular
repository, under a different URL. Existing tools are not affected.

## How to teach

Users will not see these files.

## Unresolved questions

None currently.

## Alternatives

### Per-day `PACKAGES` files

P3M already serves a full `PACKAGES` file for every day. A client
could download these, but finding all versions of a package, or the
first snapshot of a version, would need thousands of downloads.

### An index of all binaries

A single file listing every binary of every package would be very
large for CRAN (cli alone has over 3,000 rows), and almost all of it
would be irrelevant for any one project. One small file per package means
a client only downloads what it needs, and the requests can run in
parallel.

### JSON instead of DCF and TSV

JSON would be easier to parse with general tools, but DCF is what R
and existing R tools already read, and `ALLPACKAGES` is a valid
`PACKAGES` file. TSV keeps the binary indices small and fast to parse.
